tools.name: Input_emulateTouchFromMouseEvent
tools.description: Send one touch gesture event to a Lynx page. For a tap, send mousePressed then mouseReleased at the same coordinates with button left, using the same clientId and sessionId. For a drag, send mouseMoved events between press and release. Send events sequentially with nondecreasing timestamps; after a press, attempt release even if a later gesture step fails. Get coordinates from DOM_getBoxModel and validate the target with DOM_getNodeForLocation before pressing.

clientId.description: Target client ID returned by Device_listClients. Pass it through unchanged.

sessionId.description: Target session_id returned by Device_listSessions for the selected clientId. Pass it through unchanged.

type.description: Gesture phase: mousePressed starts a touch, mouseMoved moves a pressed touch, and mouseReleased ends it.

x.description: Horizontal coordinate in CDP logical units, in the same coordinate space as DOM_getBoxModel and DOM_getNodeForLocation. Screenshot pixels are not interchangeable.

y.description: Vertical coordinate in CDP logical units, in the same coordinate space as DOM_getBoxModel and DOM_getNodeForLocation. Screenshot pixels are not interchangeable.

timestamp.description: Event timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as returned by Date.now().

instructions:
The Lynx DevTool MCP Server provides tools to interact with Lynx-based applications.

Glossary:
  1. Device: The DevTool MCP Server can connect to multiple devices (simulators or real devices).
  2. Client: A device can have multiple clients (Lynx applications) opened.
  3. Session: Each client may open multiple sessions (e.g., Lynx pages with same or different URLs).

Tool selection guidance:
  1. All tools have name '<DOMAIN>_<METHOD_NAME>'. <DOMAIN> is the domain of the tool, e.g., 'CSS', 'DOM', 'Debugger', 'Runtime', etc. Most of the tools would have the same functionality with Chrome DevTools Protocol. See documentation at: https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/<DOMAIN>/#method-<METHOD_NAME>.

Tool usage guidance:
  1. Most of the tools would require a 'clientId' and a 'sessionId' parameter to identify the target client and session. You can get the list of connected devices, clients and sessions using the 'Device.listDevices', 'Device.listClients' and 'Device.listSessions' tools.
